blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Re-reviewed 2026-07-22: DebtToken.burn(account, amount) is callable by enabled TroveManagers and the owner-configured lending-vault adapter without holder allowance. Those protocol-authorized paths can destroy an arbitrary holder balance, so true replaces the prior inherited-only posture. The same DebtToken address is tracked across deployments.

oracleRisk.summary: Bima's documented USBD collateral markets use listed external oracle contracts through a shared PriceFeed that rejects stale, invalid, or greater-than-50% round changes, retains the last valid price only within the configured heartbeat, and otherwise reverts price-dependent operations.

branchApplicability.rationale: Bima deploys a distinct TroveManager for each collateral while sharing the same PriceFeed, LiquidationManager, and multi-collateral Stability Pool implementation. The official address registry maps the documented collateral markets to their external oracle contracts, so the markets are reviewed as one grouped common-engine branch with every listed active TroveManager collateral enumerated.

branches.label: Documented Bima EVM TroveManager markets
branches.summary: Nine collateral markets with published TroveManager and oracle addresses use Bima's common Liquity-derived liquidation engine and multi-collateral Stability Pool across Ethereum, Hemi, Plume, Sonic, GOAT, BSC, and Nibiru.

feeds.path: BTC/USD for Ethereum WBTC, tacBTC, and strBTC

branches.fallbackBehavior: PriceFeed accepts a new external-oracle round only when the current and previous responses are valid, the current response is within the configured per-token heartbeat, and the round-to-round change is at most 50%. Otherwise it returns the stored last valid price only while that record remains within the heartbeat; after that it reverts rather than switching providers.
branches.liquidationMechanism: Any external actor may immediately call the shared LiquidationManager for an eligible Trove. Below MCR, USBD in the Stability Pool offsets debt and depositors receive collateral; any debt and collateral not offset are redistributed to remaining active Troves, with Recovery Mode adding liquidations below system TCR.
branches.backstop: The multi-collateral Stability Pool is the first liquidation backstop. It burns deposited USBD against eligible Trove debt and credits the seized collateral to depositors; any portion beyond pool capacity is redistributed across active Troves in the same collateral market.
branches.shutdownOrBadDebtBehavior: During collateral sunsetting, new loans are disabled and Stability Pool collateral handoff is disabled, so liquidations redistribute debt and collateral to remaining active Troves. The LiquidationManager preserves one final Trove per market by design, and the reviewed contracts do not define a separate global settlement or external bad-debt fund.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: USBD has one reviewed canonical native Bima CDP issuance deployment on Ethereum and five LayerZero OFT bridge-representation routes to Hemi, Plume, Sonic, BSC, and Nibiru. The official Bima registry/source and fixed-block reads confirm local BorrowerOperations, Factory, DebtToken, and collateral-market wiring on the destination chains, but the same byte-identical regular OFT mints destination balances through authenticated LayerZero delivery and no per-chain reserve/liability reconciliation isolates those balances from incoming OFT supply. Under the conservative mint/bridge boundary, Ethereum remains the only Mint Authority deployment; the five destination routes remain Bridge Risk representations. The code-empty EOA 0xe3fbba95bb35be804696624dd1e9344a86e3cbc4 administers the OFT owner/delegate and peer/application configuration, while each LayerZero Endpoint delivery path is separately authored as the bridge-mint holder. Fixed 2026-08-16 peer reads found Ethereum peers for Hemi, Sonic, and Plume, while BSC and Nibiru's Ethereum peers were zero; current 2026-08-17 checks also found zero supply and zero local Trove debt on BSC and Nibiru. Per-application DVN/ULN, executor, endpoint-admin, and numeric route-limit settings remain evidence gaps, so the route tier remains external-validated-network.

routes.protocol: Bima USBD native issuance (Liquity-v1-fork CDP) with LayerZero OFT source/destination overlay
routes.reviewNote: Canonical USBD home deployment (27.4% of supply). Fixed-block reads at Ethereum blocks 25,770,562 and 25,770,566 (2026-08-16) confirmed local BorrowerOperations/Factory/DebtToken wiring and the documented collateralized CDP mint path. The same direct 19,637-byte DebtToken is also a regular LayerZero OFT: endpoint() = 0x1a44076050125825900e736c501f859c50fe728c and owner() = code-empty EOA 0xe3fbba95bb35be804696624dd1e9344a86e3cbc4. This route remains native for the reviewed Ethereum liability surface; its OFT inbound/outbound bridge machinery is scored separately under the endpoint and owner controls below.

At Hemi blocks 5,087,661 and 5,087,665 (2026-08-16), the official Bima registry and live reads confirmed a local BorrowerOperations/Factory/DebtToken stack and the documented iBTC collateral market; the DebtToken totalSupply was 5,447,824,812,365,803,018,146,460 while aggregate local Trove-manager debt was nonzero but not reconciled to the full destination balance. The same byte-identical DebtToken is a regular LayerZero OFT: endpoint() = 0x6f475642a6e85809b1c36fa62763669b1b48dd5b (EID 30329), peers(30101) was nonzero, and owner() = EOA 0xe3fbba95bb35be804696624dd1e9344a86e3cbc4. Because the local liability ledger does not isolate all destination supply from authenticated OFT delivery, this route is conservatively a bridge representation; the documented local CDP path is retained as evidence but is not admitted to Mint Authority.

At Plume blocks 87,682,495 and 87,682,632 (2026-08-16), the official Bima registry and live reads confirmed a local BorrowerOperations/Factory/DebtToken stack and the documented enzoBTC collateral market, but the local TroveManager getEntireSystemDebt() was 0 while DebtToken.totalSupply was 30,479,000,000,000,000. The same byte-identical DebtToken is a regular LayerZero OFT: endpoint() = 0xc1b15d3b262beec0e3565c11c9e0f6134bdacb36 (EID 30370), peers(30101) was nonzero, and owner() = EOA 0xe3fbba95bb35be804696624dd1e9344a86e3cbc4. The nonzero balance without local Trove debt is direct evidence that the destination balance cannot be treated as independently native; this route remains a bridge representation.

At Sonic blocks 77,632,123 and 77,632,147 (2026-08-16), the official Bima registry and live reads confirmed a local BorrowerOperations/Factory/DebtToken stack and the documented LBTC collateral market, but the local TroveManager getEntireSystemDebt() was 0 while DebtToken.totalSupply was 9,182,000,000,000,000. The same byte-identical DebtToken is a regular LayerZero OFT: endpoint() = 0x6f475642a6e85809b1c36fa62763669b1b48dd5b (EID 30332), the Ethereum token's peers(30332) was nonzero, and owner() = EOA 0xe3fbba95bb35be804696624dd1e9344a86e3cbc4. The nonzero balance without local Trove debt is direct evidence that the destination balance cannot be treated as independently native; this route remains a bridge representation.

At BSC blocks 116,350,940 and 116,351,071 (2026-08-16), the official Bima registry and live reads confirmed a local BorrowerOperations/Factory/DebtToken stack and the documented bfBTC collateral market; the Ethereum peer for EID 30102 was zero. A latest 2026-08-17 read at BSC block 116,455,172 returned DebtToken.totalSupply() = 0 and local TroveManager debt = 0. The same byte-identical DebtToken is a regular LayerZero OFT with endpoint() = 0x1a44076050125825900e736c501f859c50fe728c (EID 30102), owner() = EOA 0xe3fbba95bb35be804696624dd1e9344a86e3cbc4, and no fixed-block evidence proving an independent native liability ledger. This route remains conservatively a bridge representation.

At Nibiru blocks 44,572,760 and 44,572,793 (2026-08-16), the official Bima registry and live reads confirmed a local BorrowerOperations/Factory/DebtToken stack and the documented uBTC collateral market; the Ethereum peer for EID 30369 was zero. A latest 2026-08-17 read at Nibiru block 44,599,106 returned DebtToken.totalSupply() = 0 and local TroveManager debt = 0. The same byte-identical DebtToken is a regular LayerZero OFT with endpoint() = 0x2a5e79dee6e3544588bb3b675b1cc3354df2aefd (EID 30369), owner() = EOA 0xe3fbba95bb35be804696624dd1e9344a86e3cbc4, and no fixed-block evidence proving an independent native liability ledger. This route remains conservatively a bridge representation.

routeChecks.trustedPeerOrRemote: The canonical Ethereum OFT endpoint() is 0x1a44076050125825900e736c501f859c50fe728c; its authenticated delivery path accepts LayerZero messages for the configured Hemi, Sonic, and Plume peers. EIDs 30329, 30332, and 30370 were nonzero peers on the Ethereum token at block 25770566; EIDs 30102 and 30369 were zero.
routeChecks.rateLimits: No current aggregate or per-route LayerZero DVN/ULN, executor, or numeric rate-limit setting was independently replayed at the observation block.
routeChecks.onchainAmountBounds: The Ethereum DebtToken also has a local native CDP mint path. This control covers only inbound OFT delivery, which credits/mints tokens after source-side OFT debit/burn; it does not replace the separately scored BimaCore native mint control. controls.label: USBD LayerZero DVN/ULN validator authority

routeChecks.attestorQuorum: The exact per-OApp send and receive ULN libraries, required and optional DVNs, confirmation thresholds, executor settings, and validator operating authorities were not independently read for the reviewed USBD routes.
routeChecks.trustedPeerOrRemote: The exact OFT delivery Endpoints and common owner/delegate EOA are recorded in separate controls. Those delivery and application-admin identities do not establish the independent LayerZero validator authority.

controls.evidence: Current endpoint code and owner reads resolve the exact USBD delivery and peer-admin contracts separately. The reviewed evidence does not resolve the weakest external DVN/ULN validator authority for these routes, so this control remains unknown rather than inheriting an Endpoint contract identity. Reclassified 2026-09-01 under AUTHORITY-LADDER 9.46: the controlling party for this control is the external LayerZero DVN/ULN validation quorum itself, a rotating protocol-scoped operator set with no single controllerAddress to record. Its authority model is therefore validator-quorum, known but weak, graded no higher than a named issuer backend and never above a named multisig, rather than unknown. The unresolved roster, quorum, override and peer facts recorded above are unchanged; only the authority classification moved.
